title: DrivingWorld: Constructing World Model for Autonomous Driving via Video GPT

output_modality.value: single-view (front camera) video plus predicted vehicle orientation and location for the next frame

control_signal.value: vehicle orientation and ego location history, i.e. pre-defined trajectory paths, given with a short condition video clip

control_mechanism.value: pose tokenized into discrete tokens alongside image tokens in a GPT-style autoregressive model; next-frame module with multimodal fusion layer, balanced attention to keep control tokens from being diluted, random masking strategy.

base_model.value: Own 1B-parameter autoregressive world model with a 70M temporal-aware VQVAE video tokenizer (codebook 16,384); trained from scratch on driving video, not on a pretrained video backbone.

datasets.value: World model on 3456 hours: 120 h NuPlan plus 3336 h private data, fine-tuned on NuScenes; tokenizer also uses Openimages, COCO, YoutubeDV, NuPlan. Test: 200 NuPlan and 150 NuScenes clips.

metrics.value: FVD, FID, PSNR, LPIPS; FVD at 10, 25, 40 frames; planning L2 error and collision rate on NuScenes; user study against Vista.

controllability_evidence.value: User study prefers it over Vista on controllability (percentages in Fig. 8, assignment to datasets unclear); planning on NuScenes gives avg L2 1.26 m and avg collision rate 0.38 %, camera only, no auxiliary supervision.

closed_loop.value: No closed loop with a policy; open-loop long generation of 640 frames conditioned on 15 frames; up to 40 seconds in abstract. Planning evaluated open-loop on NuScenes.

stated_limitations.value: Future work: integrate multimodal and multi-view data to improve understanding and control. No explicit limitations section in packet.

notes: Inconsistent duration claims: 40 s (abstract), 64 s at 10 Hz (Sec 4.3), 128 s at 5 Hz (Fig 7 caption). Controllability numbers in user study not mapped to dataset.
